topics.name: Passive voice (simple present, past and future)

options: Pens will be provide in the hall.
Pens will be provided in the hall.
Pens will provided in the hall.
questions.rule: Future passive = will be + past participle: will be provided.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: The institute has issued a list of rules.
The institute have issued a list of rules.
The institute has issue a list of rules.
questions.rule: Present perfect = has/have + past participle. One institute takes has issued.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: is
was
have

questions.rule: Hundreds of people is plural, and since needs the present perfect: have gathered.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: allowing
allowed
allows

questions.rule: Passive needs the past participle: will not be allowed.

questions.before: Climate change is one of the
options: biggest
bigger
most big
questions.rule: one of the + superlative: one of the biggest problems.

options: were
be
was
questions.rule: After said that, 'am' moves back to was. She takes was, not 'were'.

options: Yes, I have read it already.
Yes, I have readed it already.
Yes, I has read it already.
questions.rule: I have + past participle. The past participle of read is read.

chat: Can we take our own pens into the hall?
options: No, pens are give by the invigilators.
No, pens are given by the invigilators.
No, pens is given by the invigilators.
questions.rule: Present passive: are + past participle. Plural pens takes are given.
Present perfect: has + past participle = has finished.

options: Ritika said that she was tired.
Ritika said that I was tired.
Ritika said that she were tired.
questions.rule: I becomes she, and am moves back to was.

options: Earplugs were banned in the exam hall.
Earplugs was banned in the exam hall.
Earplugs were ban in the exam hall.
questions.rule: Past passive: plural earplugs + were + past participle banned.

options: Hawking said that the planet need protection.
Hawking said that the planet needed protection.
Hawking said that the planet needing protection.
questions.rule: In reported speech after said, the verb moves back: needs becomes needed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: willing
wanting
would

questions.rule: After told (past) and with the next day, will changes to would in reported speech.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: much
many
most

questions.rule: Of all compares more than two, so use the superlative: the most serious.

options: was printed
is printed
printed
questions.rule: Yesterday needs the past; the news did not print itself, so use the passive was printed.

questions.after: increased in the last few weeks.
options: have
has
is
questions.rule: The subject is the number (singular), so use has increased.

options: The pens were provided by the invigilators.
The pens are provided by the invigilators.
The pens are provide by the invigilators.
questions.rule: Simple present passive: are + past participle. Keep the present tense: are provided.

options: Miribaba said that I sold the powder.
Miribaba said that he selled the powder.
Miribaba said that he sold the powder.
questions.rule: I becomes he; sell moves back to sold (not 'selled').
Past passive: was + past participle = was read.

chat: What did the reporter say about the queue?
options: She said that it were very long.
She said that it is very longer.
She said that it was very long.
questions.rule: Reported statement: is becomes was; it takes was.

options: Closed shoes must not be wear in the hall.
Closed shoes must not be worn in the hall.
Closed shoes must not been worn in the hall.
questions.rule: Modal passive: must not be + past participle = must not be worn.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Ritika signed the film last month.
Ritika has signed the film last month.
Ritika has sign the film last month.
questions.rule: A finished past time like last month takes the simple past, not the present perfect: signed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: written
writing
writes

questions.rule: Present perfect = have + past participle: have written (not 'wrote').

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: gave
given
gives

questions.rule: The pens receive the action (by the invigilators), so use the passive: were given.

questions.before: The reporter told us that she
options: has
have
had
questions.rule: The day before shows an earlier past in reported speech: had visited.
told + person + that + backshifted verb: she was quitting.
Long adjectives form the superlative with the most: the most dangerous.

chat: Is Kabir still at the exam centre?
options: No, he has just leave.
No, he have just left.
No, he has just left.
questions.rule: just often goes with the present perfect: he has just left.

chat: Which is faster for news, TV or the newspaper?
options: TV is the faster than the newspaper.
TV is fastest than the newspaper.
TV is faster than the newspaper.
questions.rule: Two things compared: comparative + than, with no 'the': faster than.

questions.source: The institute has issued the rules.
options: The institute has not issued the rules.
The institute has not issue the rules.
The institute did not issued the rules.
questions.rule: Present perfect negative: has not + past participle = has not issued.

options: An entrance test will be held in May.
A entrance test will be held in May.
An entrance test will be hold in May.
questions.rule: An before a vowel sound (entrance); future passive will be held.

options: The rules have changed, didn't they?
The rules have changed, haven't they?
The rules have changed, haven't it?
questions.rule: The tag uses the helper have and a matching pronoun: haven't they?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: longer
longest
length

questions.rule: than needs the comparative: longer than.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: were
is
be

questions.rule: Each + singular noun takes a singular verb: each packet is blessed.

options: since
for
from
questions.rule: A length of time (ten years) takes for with the present perfect.

options: can't
cannot
could
questions.rule: In reported speech can moves back to could: could not use. 'can't not' is a double negative.

options: Ritika was interviewed by a journalist.
Ritika is interviewed by a journalist.
Ritika was interview by a journalist.
questions.rule: Simple past active becomes was + past participle: was interviewed.

options: TV is not as cheap as radio.
TV is not as cheaper as radio.
Radio is not as cheap as TV.
questions.rule: Swap the two and use not as + plain adjective + as: TV is not as cheap as radio.
Future passive: will be + past participle + by + doer.

chat: What did Dr Karnik tell the reporter?
options: He told her that more patients had came to the hospital.
He told her that more patients had come to the hospital.
He said her that more patients had come to the hospital.
questions.rule: told her (not 'said her') + past perfect had come.

options: The candidates was told that they would not be allowed to carry pens.
The candidates were told that they would not be allow to carry pens.
The candidates were told that they would not be allowed to carry pens.
questions.rule: Plural candidates were told, and modal passive would not be allowed.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tenses.
options: Ever since the news came out, fewer people visited Ralewadi.
Ever since the news came out, fewer people have visited Ralewadi.
Ever since the news has come out, fewer people visited Ralewadi.
questions.rule: Ever since + past point (came out), then present perfect in the main clause: have visited.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: much
most
many

questions.rule: the ... ever compares with all times, so use the superlative: the most dangerous.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: issuing
issued
issues

questions.rule: Present perfect passive: has been + past participle = has been issued.

questions.before: Ritika told the journalists that she
questions.after: sign any more films after her next one.
options: will not to
not will
would not
questions.rule: After told, will not moves back to would not + base verb.
Reported statement: is facing moves back to was facing.

chat: Why are so many people waiting in the sun?
options: Yes, a powder is being sell by a man who says it cures everything.
Yes, a powder is being sold by a man which says it cures everything.
Yes, a powder is being sold by a man who says it cures everything.
questions.rule: Continuous passive: is being + past participle = is being sold. Use who for a man.

chat: Have you ever written a letter to the Principal?
options: Yes, I have written one last year about our class bulletin.
Yes, I have wrote one last year about our class bulletin.
Yes, I wrote one last year about our class bulletin.
questions.rule: Last year is a finished time, so the answer uses the simple past: I wrote one.

questions.source: The invigilator said to the candidates, "You must switch off your phones."
options: The invigilator told the candidates that they had to switch off their phones.
The invigilator told the candidates that they has to switch off their phones.
The invigilator told the candidates that you had to switch off your phones.
questions.rule: said to becomes told; you/your become they/their; must becomes had to.

questions.source: No other actress in Bollywood is paid as highly as Ritika.
options: Ritika is the most highly paid actress in Bollywood.
Ritika is the more highly paid actress in Bollywood.
Ritika is the highest paid actresses in Bollywood.
questions.rule: 'No other ... as highly as' becomes the superlative: the most highly paid actress.
